measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes Section 43 of Ansonia’s charter to require the mayor to send the proposed annual budget to the Board of Apportionment and Taxation by the second Monday in March. If a public budget referendum is needed, it must be held 10 to 14 calendar days after the Board of Aldermen approves the budget.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the March budget deadline and the 10 to 14 day referendum window.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject these proposed budget deadlines.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Requires a public referendum on Ansonia’s budget whenever the Board of Aldermen approves total spending at least 4% above the previous fiscal year.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Require a public budget vote when that spending threshold is reached.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed requirement for a public budget vote.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes Section 129 of Ansonia’s charter to replace the title Fire Superintendent with Fire Chief. It also establishes a process for selecting the second Fire Chief and specifies who appoints members of the Board of Fire Commissioners.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these changes to fire department titles, selection and appointments.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject these proposed fire department charter changes.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Removes Section 130 of Ansonia’s charter, which concerns the obsolete Superintendent of Fire Alarms position.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Remove the charter section for the obsolete position.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject removal of this charter section.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Regional School District 10 to spend $5 million on replacing and improving heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems at district schools. It authorizes bonds and temporary borrowing for the same amount.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve spending and borrowing $5 million for this school project.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Regional School District 10 to spend $14.935 million on replacing and improving roofs at Lewis S. Mills High School, Lake Garda School and Har-Bur Middle School. It authorizes bonds and temporary borrowing for the same amount.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve spending and borrowing $14.935 million for this school project.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Regional School District 10 to spend $3.9 million on installing a multipurpose field with synthetic turf, with related improvements, at Lewis S. Mills High School. It authorizes bonds and temporary borrowing for the same amount.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve spending and borrowing $3.9 million for this school project.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Regional School District 10 to spend $3.1 million on installing a multipurpose field with engineered natural grass, with related improvements, at Lewis S. Mills High School. It authorizes bonds and temporary borrowing for the same amount.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve spending and borrowing $3.1 million for this school project.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Cheshire to spend $1.1 million on a replacement salt shed at the Public Works Garage and issue bonds and notes for that amount. Any project grants received would reduce the borrowing.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this project spending and borrowing, reduced by project grants.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this project spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Cheshire to spend $2.35 million on the Road Improvement Program and issue bonds and notes for that amount. Any project grants received would reduce the borrowing.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this project spending and borrowing, reduced by project grants.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this project spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Cheshire to spend $1.375 million on reconstructing Dickerman Road and issue bonds and notes for that amount. Any project grants received would reduce the borrowing.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this project spending and borrowing, reduced by project grants.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this project spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Cheshire to spend $1 million on buying land for recreation, open space, conservation, education or municipal purposes, or a combination of those uses and issue bonds and notes for that amount. Any project grants received would reduce the borrowing.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this project spending and borrowing, reduced by project grants.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this project spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Cheshire to spend $875,000 on safety and drainage improvements at the Cheshire High School loading dock and issue bonds and notes for that amount. Any project grants received would reduce the borrowing.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this project spending and borrowing, reduced by project grants.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this project spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Clinton to spend and borrow $3.32 million for capital projects: $195,000 for a Public Works wheeled excavator, $125,000 for a Police Department generator, $1 million for roads and sidewalks, and $2 million for library renovations. The library work includes related surveys, alterations, repairs and improvements, engineering, architecture, and temporary and permanent financing costs. The town could issue bonds, notes or other obligations to pay for the projects.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the listed capital projects and $3.32 million borrowing authorization.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this package of capital project spending and borrowing.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes the threshold for requiring a town meeting, a referendum, or both to approve spending or borrowing. Instead of a fixed dollar amount, the threshold would be a percentage of the current tax levy. Charter Sections 9-3(a) and 9-3(e) would be renumbered 7-3(a) and 7-3(d).
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve using a percentage of the current tax levy for this approval threshold.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed change to the approval threshold.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increases Durham’s Board of Selectmen from 3 members to 5 by changing the town charter.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve a Board of Selectmen with 5 members.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject expanding the Board of Selectmen.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes Durham’s Town Clerk and Tax Collector positions from elected offices to appointed offices.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Make both positions appointed.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject changing these positions from elected to appointed.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Enfield to spend $511 million to build new Hazardville Memorial, Prudence Crandall, Parkman and Barnard elementary schools and convert Eli Whitney Elementary School into the Eagle Academy Therapeutic Day School. The town could borrow up to $89 million through bonds or notes; grants and other available money would cover the rest.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the school construction and conversion plan, including up to $89 million in town borrowing.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this school spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Approves $30.426 million in spending and bonds for the Middletown Public Schools Districtwide Infrastructure Project.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this school infrastructure spending and borrowing.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this school infrastructure spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Requires elected and appointed New Canaan town officers with management authority to follow applicable town policies, ethics standards and lawful administrative directions. They would answer to the First Selectman on administration and operations unless doing so conflicts with their authority under state law.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these management, ethics and accountability requirements.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject these proposed charter requirements.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Requires Town Council confirmation of appointments to New Canaan’s Planning and Zoning Commission.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Give the Town Council approval authority over these appointments.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed confirmation requirement.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Requires Town Council approval for changes to real property owned by New Canaan.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Require Town Council approval for these property changes.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed approval requirement.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Removes the requirement that New Canaan Board of Finance members be taxpayers on real property.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Remove the real property taxpayer requirement for Board of Finance membership.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject removing that membership requirement.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds 3 alternate members to New Canaan’s Ethics Board.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve adding 3 alternate Ethics Board members.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject adding these alternate members.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Newington to spend up to $7.8 million to build a new Fire Station 4 at 84 Fifth Street. It authorizes general obligation bonds or notes of up to $7.8 million, with borrowing reduced by project grants.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this fire station spending and borrowing, reduced by grants.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this fire station spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Approves $55 million in spending and bonds to plan, acquire and build the Norwich Police Headquarters Facility Project at 300 Main Street downtown.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this police headquarters spending and borrowing.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this police headquarters spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Expands Plainfield’s Board of Selectmen from 3 members to 5 starting with the November 2027 town election.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve expanding the board at the November 2027 election.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed board expansion.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Plainfield’s Board of Police Commissioners, by a majority vote, to hire its own lawyer separately from Town Counsel. The board must decide that separate representation is needed for its legal, disciplinary, investigative, administrative or oversight duties, including conflicts of interest.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Allow the police commission to hire separate legal counsel under these conditions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed authority for separate legal counsel.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Raises the grant matching approval limit in Plainfield Charter Section 2-5(d) from $10,000 to $35,000.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the $35,000 approval limit for grant matching funds.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject raising this approval limit.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Requires Plainfield to use money received through an awarded grant only for the purpose stated in that grant.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Require grant money to be used only for its stated purpose.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed charter restriction on grant money.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows South Windsor to spend and borrow $15 million to plan, design, build or replace road paving, traffic signals, safety devices, culverts, sidewalks and drainage improvements throughout town.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the $15 million spending and bond authorization for these improvements.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Southington to spend and borrow $86,675,560 for its Elementary Facilities Plan. The work includes a new Kelley Elementary School, fitting out South End Elementary School, and closing Flanders Elementary School and reusing its building and property for municipal and community purposes.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the elementary school plan and its spending and borrowing authorization.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this spending and borrowing authorization for the plan.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Tolland to spend $6.5 million on roof improvements and replacement of the artificial turf field at Tolland High School. It authorizes general obligation bonds and notes for the same amount.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the high school roof and field spending and borrowing.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this high school spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes West Haven’s charter to give the Mayor and Town and City Clerk terms of 4 years starting with the 2027 municipal election.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve terms of 4 years for these offices starting in 2027.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed change to these terms of office.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Replaces the charter chapter on the Village Improvement Association, known as the VIA, with provisions governing its operation of the public library as a separate nonprofit organization. The new provisions address its responsibilities, budget obligations and accountability to the city.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the replacement charter provisions for the VIA’s library operations.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject replacing these library charter provisions.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Changes Weston’s limit on representation by the majority political party on boards and commissions. Instead of a bare majority, that party could hold up to the maximum number of seats allowed by state law, C.G.S. 9-167a.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve using the state law maximum for majority party representation.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed change to party representation limits.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Removes the Annual Town Budget Meeting’s power to reduce or eliminate budget items before the budget goes directly to voters in a referendum for approval or rejection.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Remove the budget meeting’s power to cut items before the referendum.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed removal of the budget meeting’s power.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Wethersfield to spend and borrow up to $4 million to buy a ladder truck and a rescue truck for its Fire Department.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve buying the two fire trucks with up to $4 million in spending and borrowing.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this fire truck spending and borrowing authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Makes Winchester’s Town Clerk a position appointed by the Town Manager, effective January 3, 2028.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve appointment of the Town Clerk by the Town Manager starting January 3, 2028.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed change to selection of the Town Clerk.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Extends Winchester’s Registrar of Voters term to 4 years, effective January 3, 2029.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve a term of 4 years starting January 3, 2029.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed term change.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Limits an elector to serving on only one of these Winchester boards: Board of Selectmen, Board of Education, Zoning Board of Appeals, Inland Wetlands and Watercourses Commission, Board of Assessment Appeals, Water and Sewer Commission, or Planning and Zoning Commission.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve limiting an elector to membership on only one of the listed boards.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed limit on membership across these boards.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds charter definitions of elector and property owner. Only electors would be allowed to hold elected town office or serve on any town board, commission, agency or committee.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these definitions and the elector requirement for town offices and bodies.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject these proposed definitions and eligibility restrictions.
